title: WPSS/1859/2018 of Smt. Daya Pandey Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.1859 of 2018

Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö.ÖRespondents
Present:- Mr. D.K. Joshi, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Narain Dutt, Brief Holder, for the Sate/respondent nos.1 to 4
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate, for the respondent no.5.

Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner was a candidate for the post of
ìAganbadi Karyakartiî for the ìAganbadi Centre Munauoliî.
It is an admitted fact that for the appointment on the post
of ìAganbadi Karyakartiî, one of the conditions is that the
candidate must have a high school certificate and
preference is given to a widow. The petitioner falls in this
preferential category inasmuch as she is a widow.
Thereafter, the Evaluation Committee considered the case
of the petitioner amongst other candidates and the
petitioner was declared selected. Thereafter a complaint
was made to the Child Development Project Officer, Dhola
Dev, Almora, who has passed the impugned order dated
16.04.2018 stating therein that when the petitioner was
working as ìAganbadi Sahayikaî she has done her high
school through distance mode, for which she has not taken
any prior permission from the concerned authority. On this
ground, the selection of the petitioner has been put in
abeyance and it was directed that the petitioner shall
remain posted as ìAganbadi Sahayikaî. This order dated
16.04.2018, the petitioner has challenged before this
Court.

2
2. One of the preliminary objections raised by
the learned counsel for respondent no.5 is that as per the
Government Order dated 24.02.2009 there is an Appellate
Authority where the petitioner can approach. However, in
this case the petitioner cannot be relegated to the Appellate
Authority inasmuch as process for cancellation of the
appointment of the petitioner has not been fair procedure
and the principles of natural justice and fair play have been
violated. It is an admitted case of the State that before
passing the impugned order dated 16.04.2018, no
opportunity of hearing was given to the petitioner.
3. In any case, the candidature of the petitioner
has been rejected on an absolutely trivial issue. The
petitioner was not holding a civil post for which she could
have taken the permission for sitting in the high school
examination from ìdistance modeî, as the petitioner has
done all her studies while working as ìAganbadi Sahayikaî.
4. In view of the above, the writ petition is
allowed. The order dated 16.04.2018 passed by respondent
no.4 is hereby quashed.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 27.11.2018
Nitesh/
